• Put the phone in a holder. A loose phone gives noisy readings.
• Tap START before you drive (or set up Auto start). It keeps running with the screen off.
• First pass over a bump: a soft tick as it is recorded. After that: 2 high beeps before you reach it (3 above 50 km/h). Potholes: 2 low bongs; harsh ones: a voice says which side they're on. Not sure yet what it is: 1 beep. Several close together: the voice says e.g. "3 bumps ahead".
• Bump or pothole is judged from how the car moves; each pass makes it surer. Correct any spot on the Map tab.
• A spot you pass 3+ times but rarely feel is muted automatically. "Mute last warning" silences a false alarm.
• Your driving score (Trips tab) looks at speeding, harsh braking, cornering, swerving, speed bumps taken fast and phone use.
• Everything stays on your phone. Share only what you choose.

Drive at least 0.5 km with recording on to get a score.
Your score looks at speeding, harsh braking and acceleration, harsh cornering, swerving, speed bumps taken fast, and handling the phone while driving.

Every trip starts at 100. Points come off for:

• Speeding: time above your limit (Settings → Driving score), more the further over. With real speed limits on and known for at least half the trip: time over each road's limit by +10, +20 and +30 km/h instead.
• Harsh braking (over ≈0.35 g) and harsh acceleration (over ≈0.3 g).
• Harsh cornering (over ≈0.4 g sideways) and swerves (a sudden left-right).
• Speed bumps from your map taken faster than 25 km/h.
• Picking up the phone while moving.

Events are counted per 10 km, so long trips aren't punished for being long; trips under 5 km count as 5 km. Trips under 0.5 km get no score. Your overall score is the distance-weighted average of your last 20 trips.

90+ Excellent · 75+ Good · 60+ Fair · below 60 Needs work.

Score speeding against each road\'s real limit (from TomTom), looked up after the trip. Needs the internet. When off or unknown, the speed above is used.

After each trip, the app sends your route to our server, which asks TomTom for the speed limits on those roads. The first and last 300 m of every trip are never sent. TomTom doesn\'t get your phone ID or internet (IP) address: it only sees our server. Our server keeps nothing except a daily count of lookups, deleted after 30 days. The route waits on your phone until it\'s looked up. After about 2 days it is never sent, and it\'s deleted the next time the app runs. You can turn this off at any time.
Until you answer the shared-map question, the app sends nothing to our server (it only checks GitHub for updates). Choose “Share and receive” or “Receive only” first, then turn on real speed limits.

Bump Beeper collects location data to notice when you start driving and to start recording without Bluetooth, even when the app is closed or not in use.

It uses the motion sensor, short GPS checks and location updates that other apps already asked for. All of this is checked on your phone.

Your location stays on the phone, unless you turned on the shared map, real speed limits or “Help improve detection” (see the privacy policy). You can turn this off at any time in Settings.
Android will now open Bump Beeper\'s location settings. Choose “%1$s” there, then come back. Without it, recording can\'t start while the app is closed.
On the next screen, choose “Allow all the time”. Without it, recording can\'t start while the app is closed.
Let it run in the background

Some phones stop apps that wait in the background. On the next screen, allow Bump Beeper to ignore battery optimisation so it notices when you drive. It only checks GPS briefly when the phone starts moving.
With the “Physical activity” permission, Google Play services tells Bump Beeper when you are in a vehicle. It works better and needs no notification. Without it, the built-in detection is used.

Off by default and separate from the shared map. Sends short motion-sensor samples, never your route.

This is separate from the shared map, and off unless you turn it on.

For each possible bump the app judges: up to 4 seconds of motion-sensor readings (2 s before and after) (shake, plus rotation if the phone has a gyroscope), the app's decision and its reason, speed, heading change, GPS accuracy and where the phone sits. Only the date of the drive, no time of day. Also your Android version, app version and phone brand (not the model).

For each trip: date, duration, distance, counts, beeps, score figures and battery.

No route and no coordinates. The only place information is the number of a public, confirmed bump you passed, and never within 300 m of where a trip starts or ends. Over time these can hint at the areas you drive in.

A random ID that changes each time you turn this on; on our server it is kept with this phone's anonymous record, so it can be deleted. Samples aren't linked to trips.

Uploads 1 to 6 hours after a drive, about 30 to 90 KB per drive. Kept 7 days on the phone if not sent, and 12 months on our server (Supabase, Frankfurt). Used only to improve detection, analysed offline by the app's owner, never sold.

Turning this off, or “Delete my shared data”, deletes it on the server at once, except the provider's backups and logs, which rotate.

Trips that started by themselves are held until you confirm them.
